LESSON: READING 10.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: SHORT STORY

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.4: Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: how the events in the short story relate to real life. 1. How do events flow logically in a story?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the setting in the short story
2. appreciate the importance of literature in life

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 10.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: SHORT STORY
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 10.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: SHORT STORY
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify the setting in the short story

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the setting in the short story. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the setting in the short story.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the setting in the short story. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the importance of literature in life

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of literature in life. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of literature in life.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of literature in life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify the setting in the short story)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story to a partner. (skill: appreciate the importance of literature in life)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the setting in the short story.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance of literature in life.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. how the events in the short story relate to real life. 1. How do events flow logically in a story?
2. Why is the setting of a story important to the reader?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the setting in the short story.
5. Be able to: appreciate the importance of literature in life.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
